texts.preamble: Madhu B.S vs Siddresh Kumar B.R on 1 September, 2025 Kabc020262592022 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru . Mvc No.4803/2022 Dated this 1st day of September, 2025 Petitioner: Madhu B.S. S/o Late Siddaiah, Aged about 30 years, Residing at No.35, 5th Cross, Bank Colony, Rajeshwarinagar, Laggere, Peenya Post, Bengaluru - 560 058. Permanent Address: Maruthinagar, Thavarekere Road, Bukkapattana, Sira Taluk, Tumkur - 572 115. (Sri B. Ramesha, Advocate) Vs. Respondents: 1. Siddresh Kumar B.R. S/o Rajanna, No.886, 915, M.P.M. Layout, I.T.I. Layout, Bengaluru - 560 056. 2 Mvc No.4803/2022 (Rc owner of Jupiter two-wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925) (Sri Prem Kumar B., Advocate) Madhu B.S vs Siddresh Kumar B.R on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159302214/ 1 2. Go Digit General Insurance Ltd., Atlantis, 95, 4th 'B' Cross Road, Koramangala Industrial Layout 5th Block, Bengaluru - 560 095. (Policy No. Irdan158Rp000/V01201718, valid from 08-03-2022 to 07-03-2024) (Sri B. Anjaneyalu, Advocate) Judgment
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 18-07-2022 at about 9.15 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on a Jupiter two-wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA- 41-EL-7925 as a pillion rider, the same was ridden by its rider-cum-RC owner by name Siddesh Kumar, on Bukkapattana-Hagalavadi road, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations. While so proceeding, at about 9.15 p.m., when they were infront of petrol bunk, Bukkapattana, Tumakuru, due to his rash and negligent riding, the said rider lost control over his scooter and dashed to a pedestrian. Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sira Government Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to District Hospital, Tumakur, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident, he was working as Electrician and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Sira Police have registered the case against the rider of the said two-wheeler, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements. 4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. He has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and Madhu B.S vs Siddresh Kumar B.R on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159302214/ 2 treatment taken by him. Further, he has contended that, he was riding his Jupiter two-wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 on Bukkapattana-Hagalavadi road, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations and while so proceeding, infront of Petrol bunk, Bukkapattana, Tumkur, due to big pit holes on the road, he lost control over his scooter and it skidded. Further he has contended that, he is the RC owner of the said Jupiter two- wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 and the same was insured with the respondent No.2/Go Digit General Insurance Co. Ltd., vide policy No.D058947704/07032022 valid from 08-03-2022 to 07-03-2024. The policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 18-07-2022 and he was possessing valid and effective driving licence vide D.L. No.KA4120140018713, valid from 25-11-2014 to 24-11-2034. If this Court comes to conclusion in granting any compensation to the petitioner, the respondent No.2/insurance company itself is liable to pay. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of two-wheeler package insurance policy bide No.D058947704/07032022 in respect of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 in favour of respondent No.1 and it was valid from 08-03-2022 to 07-03-2024. It has contended that, there was delay of 9 days in reporting the alleged accident to the police, as the alleged accident is said to have taken place on 18-07-2022 and the same is reported to the police on 29-07-2022. The insured scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 is falsely implicated in the alleged accident, with a sole intention to help the petitioner to get illegal and wrongful gain from the respondents. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him. As per the private investigation taken up by the respondent No.2 through its panel investigator, the police without proper investigation appear to have deliberately registered the alleged accident case against the respondent No.1, to help the petitioner to have illegal and wrongful gain by way of compensation. The petitioner is not entitled to seek for any compensation from the respondents for his own negligence and self-accident. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed: ISSUES 1. 7. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined the Investigator of the company, Police Sub- Inspector of Sira Police Station, its Associate Manager and Orthopaedic Surgeon General Hospital Sira, as R.W.1 to R.W.4 respectively and got marked total 12 Madhu B.S vs Siddresh Kumar B.R on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159302214/ 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 12.
texts.arguments: Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. It has contended that, the alleged accident, if any, was self accident by the petitioner, as he was rider of the insured Jupiter scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 at the time of alleged accident. The petitioner had no valid driving licence and he was not authorized to ride the two-wheeler on the road. Further it is contended that, the alleged injuries suffered by the petitioner are simple in nature, the said injuries have healed up, there is no any deformity or disability suffered by him and he is capable to discharge his routine and normal duties and activities. The petitioner has not suffered any loss of income. Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. The petitioner himself was the rider of the insured two- wheeler scooter at the time of the alleged accident, he had no valid driving licence authorizing him to ride the vehicle and he was not wearing safety helmet, . The respondent No.1/owner of the insured two-wheeler has willfully entrusted the vehicle to the petitioner, who had no valid driving licence and thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy. As such the respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify the owner of the insured motorcycle or pay any compensation to the petitioner arising out of the alleged accident. Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. Further in its additional written Madhu B.S vs Siddresh Kumar B.R on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159302214/ 3 statement, it has contended that, apart from the present claim there is one more petition filed by Madhusudhan in MVC No.1214/2022 in respect of the same accident before the Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. CJM, Tumkur, which is pending before the said Court. The petitioner in the present case was himself riding the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EL-7925 at the time of alleged accident on 18- 07-2022 and hit to the pedestrian, due to which the pedestrian and the petitioner in this present case are sustained injuries. But, the petitioner has been allegedly shown as pillion rider on the offending motorcycle, in order to enable him to claim compensation. The accused cum owner of insured scooter namely Siddesh Kumar B.R. has been implanted in the alleged accident as rider of said vehicle, by swapping the actual rider Madhusudhan/petitioner in the present case, in order to claim compensation from the respondent No.2 insurance company, by misrepresenting the real facts of the alleged accident. Further it is contended that, it has investigated the claim petitions through investigator, during the course of investigation the investigator has sought the mobile of the accused and verified the timeline from google map application, in order to know the tower trace location of the accused and found that, he has was not present at the place of accident, at the time of alleged accident, but he was in Bengaluru, which is around 145 km away from the place of accident. Further it is contended that, the officer from the insurance company has requested the Superintendent of Police, Tumkur, about the call details records (CDR) and tower location of the insured cum accused Siddesh Kumar B.R., on alleged date of accident i.e. 18-07-2022, through RPAD letter on 26-07-2023, which is duly served on on 31-07- 2023. But till today the respondent No.2 has not received any call details or reply from either the concerned Superintendent of Police or concerned Police Station. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has relied on the following decisions in support of his arguments: i) Ganesh Achar V/s United India Insurance Co. Ltd. and another, in MFA No.8145/2012 (MV- I), dated 03-10-2023. ii) Mahadevi and others V/s Shivaputra and another, in MFA No.201689/2016 (MV), dated 20-11-2020. iii) M/s National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Shamshad and others, in MFA No.6641/2017 (MV-D), dated 23-02-2023. Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011)4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases. The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR. Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition." In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, Madhu B.S vs Siddresh Kumar B.R on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159302214/ 8 The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 21. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
